learn.title: Recursion fits trees
learn.body: A tree is a node with smaller trees below it. So functions on trees are often recursive: handle the node, then call yourself on a subtree. The base case is NULL, an empty tree.

learn.title: Search
learn.body: Returns 1 when v is found. Each call goes one level deeper in one direction only.

learn.title: Insert
learn.body: Returns the root of the tree. When it reaches NULL, it makes the new node there. Equal values are ignored.

learn.title: Inserting 6 into the tree
steps: 6 is greater than 5, so go right to 8
6 is less than 8, so go left
8's left is NULL, so a new node 6 is created there
Each parent pointer is reassigned to itself, so the tree stays linked

learn.title: Shape matters
learn.body: Searching takes a number of steps equal to the levels it passes. If values arrive already sorted, every insert goes right, and the tree becomes a chain as slow as a list. Random order usually gives a bushy tree.

questions.prompt: What is the base case of the recursive search?
questions.explanation: An empty tree cannot contain anything, so the answer is 0.

questions.prompt: Why does `insert` return the node pointer?
choices: So the parent can store the possibly new child
questions.explanation: If t was NULL, the new node must be attached by the caller: `t->left = insert(t->left, v)`.

questions.prompt: Insert 6 into the tree with 5, 3, 8, 1, 4. Which value is its parent?
questions.explanation: 6 goes right of 5, then left of 8, becoming 8's left child.

questions.prompt: What do you get by inserting 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 in that order?
questions.explanation: Each value is larger than all before, so it always goes right.

questions.prompt: Searching a BST looks at one \_\_ per level.
questions.explanation: At each node it compares once and moves to one child.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of `insert(t, v)` when t is not NULL.
steps: Choose the left or right child
Store the result in the child pointer
questions.explanation: The recursion returns the subtree's root, which goes back into the child pointer.
